text: "We all wanted the best for the movie," Sennott says, "so there were moments where it was difficult as friends. You can't every day be like, 'Queen, I love you.'"

text: "I think all the Disney stuff and Marvel stuff... All that stuff's made for children. All this like, spinoff Marvel stuff? Made for kids. I can't watch it. Cause I'm an adult. And I find it to be like, dumb. And simple. Which is fine - I don't mind that it's made for kids. I think it's important that there is like, incredibly high production stuff that's made for kids now. And Disney has the cash flow for it, and it's great. But it isn't deep. It can't be taken seriously - it doesn't want to be taken seriously. It's all, like, it's very sarcastic. Marvel stuff is so sarcastic, and like, rolling its eyes at itself, never taking itself that seriously. It's just a brand, you know? It's a franchise. I think it's amazing that they're tapping into that, because there's some really great, imaginative writers behind that stuff, like when you look at who was writing the stuff and drawing it. But it's... Comic books. It's for kids, it's not deep. Sorry, I went off the rails there for a second."
caption: Unattributed remarks on Disney and Marvel films.

text: "Visibility these days seems to somehow equate to success. Do not be afraid to disappear, from it, from us, for a while and see what comes to you in the silence."

text: "I think the best way to retire is to die."

text: "I'm often watching movies in order to see dead people. I want to see them again, I want to hear them. And so cinema is in a way a kind of shrouded post-death machine, you know. In a way cinema is a cemetery."
